sha256_of_archive_note: Manifest digest = sha256 over sorted lines "<file sha256>  <relative path>\n". Only the test split was fetched; MAUD_train.csv (81.3 MB) and MAUD_dev.csv (21.2 MB) were deliberately NOT fetched so this slice stays a held-out evaluation set.

shape.note: `text` is the verbatim excerpt from the merger agreement (with `<omitted>` elisions and trailing `(Page N)` markers); `answer` is the expert-adjudicated deal-point choice; `label` is its integer index within the question's answer space.

what_ground_truth.a_typed_anchor_extraction: MODERATE, and uniquely valuable for DURATION NORMALIZATION. Five deal points carry expert-normalized duration answers that explicitly separate business days from calendar days and from months: 'Initial matching rights period (COR)' (73 rows), 'Initial matching rights period (FTR)' (62), 'Additional matching rights period for modifications (COR)' (64), '... (FTR)' (26), 'Tail Period Length' (64) = 289 rows. Answer vocabulary includes '3 business days', '4 business days', '5 business days', '3 calendar days', '4 calendar days', '2 business days or less', 'Greater than 5 business days', 'within 6/9/12 months'. 'Type of Consideration' (62 rows) pairs money anchors ('$177.50 in cash') with All Cash / All Stock / Mixed labels. This is bucketed-value gold, NOT a character span: the excerpt is given, the normalized duration class is the label.
what_ground_truth.b_structural_parsing: WEAK. No section tree is annotated. The excerpt text does retain section numbering ('Section 2.1(b)', '(a)', '(i)') and cross-references, which makes it good adversarial input, but there is no gold parse.

leakage_warning: LegalBench maud_* tasks and LegalBench-RAG's 'maud' benchmark are derived from this dataset. LegalBench's maud_* configs use the MAUD test split, so any model tuned on LegalBench maud_* has seen these rows. Treat MAUD as a duration-normalization probe, not as a clean holdout, if LegalBench maud_* was used anywhere upstream.
